items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: when he came to New Orleans, he made it a point to come to the Bayou Bar at the Pontchartrain Hotel and I recognized him by his pictures... he called me over, he says, I'm Barry Ulenoff

ctx.x: Okay. Now, I haven't been on the jazz scene very long, but ever since I've been on and I've been reading in jazz journals, it seems to me that you've, I've never seen a review that says anything bad about Alman Haugen. I've read the old jazz record magazine and Record Changer and Downbeat and Metronome. I really don't think that you ever had a negative review. It's a remarkable thing. Do you collect your clippings? Do you save these things? Yes.

I have tried to save most of them, Charlie, and some of them are very, very flattering and as you say, I've gotten some mighty good reviews. I think about the worst review that I ever received when you're talking about receiving bad ones was back in 1950. I cut some sides for Capital, Capital Recording Company was down there and they got a very bad setup to do it. They put up, they wanted to get an old honky-tonk style of piano and they had nothing to do with but to put an old chain across the keys, across the…
I remember correctly, I think that the A&R job was sort of leaning towards a commercial on that session too, wasn't it?
